2. Methodological Study: Why Naive Random Window Splitting Causes Data Leakage

In vibration monitoring, adjacent time windows from the same continuous acquisition share identical shaft speed, load, background noise floor, and sensor mounting resonance. Splitting windows randomly across train and test sets allows a classifier to memorize run-specific spectral signatures rather than generalizing across operating runs:

3. Physical Signal Processing: Time Domain vs. Demodulated Hilbert Envelope Spectrum

Localized defects on the outer raceway (BPFO), inner raceway (BPFI), or rolling elements (BSF / 2×BSF) produce periodic mechanical impacts that excite high-frequency structural resonances (2–5 kHz). Bandpass filtering followed by the Hilbert transform extracts the repetition rate of these impacts:

4. Explainable Single-Window Diagnostic Inspection

Physical Diagnostic Synthesis: Classified as Outer_Race_Fault (99.6% confidence). The Hilbert envelope spectrum exhibits strong harmonic energy concentration (45.5% of band energy) aligned with the Ball Pass Frequency Outer race (BPFO = 107.4 Hz, 2x = 214.7 Hz), with dominant envelope peak at 105.5 Hz and elevated waveform kurtosis (2.81).
